title: L1-L2 facet force under 400 N follower load in upright, flexion and extension

quantity.name: facet force
quantity.definition: facet contact load magnitude (compressive) with 400 N compressive follower load; upright, and at the flexion/extension angle reached in the 7.5 Nm flexibility test; mean +- SD, n=6

source.sample: 6 fresh-frozen human cadaveric T12-L2 segments screened for degeneration; facet loads at L1-L2 (gauges on L2 superior facets)

protocol.summary: Stiffness test after flexibility test: 400 N dead-weight compressive follower load (belt over pulleys, stays aligned with the specimen axis); flexion and extension induced by a hanging belt in the midsagittal plane driven by a stepper motor to the target angle determined in the flexibility test (rotation-controlled, not moment-controlled).
how_to_simulate: Fix L2; apply 400 N follower load along the T12-L2 curvature
Report L1-L2 facet force in upright posture
Rotate to the flexion and extension angles reached at 7.5 Nm without preload (displacement control) with the follower load present and report facet force
protocol.notes: Method: four-gauge strain pads on lateral L2 superior articular processes (extra-articular, capsule intact); specimen-specific neural-network models (NeuralWorks Predict) trained on post hoc calibration loads 5-125 N at up to 12 points per facet; load RMSD < 11 N (Table 1). Strain gauges cannot measure tension; values are compressive contact loads. Mean loads = 11.4% (upright), 11.6% (FL), 18.8% (EX) of the 400 N follower load (text).

data.note: digitised Fig 3; text: 11.4% of 400 N = 45.6 N

data.load: 400 N follower, flexion to 7.5 Nm angle
400 N follower, extension to 7.5 Nm angle

extraction.uncertainty: +-1 N (digitised; axis 4.56 px/N at 200 dpi; 7 bars with text values matched to within 0.2 N)
extraction.check_notes: See intact test; upright bar 45.4 N vs 11.4% x 400 N = 45.6 N.
